question: Can a large end-to-end trained neural chatbot with low perplexity be sensible and specific enough to approach human conversation, and does perplexity predict human judgement?
hypothesis: Lower test perplexity yields higher human-judged sensibleness and specificity, so a human-level chatbot may be reachable by optimising perplexity.
contributions: A simple human evaluation metric (SSA) for multi-turn open-domain chatbots
Evidence that perplexity correlates with human judgement (SSA)
Showing an end-to-end model with low enough perplexity surpasses existing handcrafted-framework chatbots on SSA

method.summary: Meena is a 2.6B Evolved Transformer seq2seq model trained on 867M (context, response) pairs from public social media, with up to 7 context turns, minimising next-token cross entropy. It is evaluated by crowd-labelled sensibleness and specificity in static (MTB) and interactive modes against Cleverbot, DialoGPT, Mitsuku, XiaoIce and humans.
method.task: open-domain multi-turn dialogue generation and its human evaluation

datasets.name: Meena social media conversations
datasets.size: 867M (context, response) pairs; 341GB text; 40B words; 61B BPE tokens
datasets.split: test perplexity reported on a held-out test set; split sizes not stated
datasets.source: mined and filtered public domain social media message trees
datasets.preprocessing: Drop message if subwords <2 or >128, alphabetic chars <70%, contains URL, username contains 'bot', repeated >100 times, high n-gram overlap with parent, unsafe per commercial classifier; remove quoted parent text; drop subtrees; 8K BPE with sentencepiece

datasets.name: Mini-Turing Benchmark (MTB)
datasets.source: Vinyals and Le (2015) questions and Loebner Prize 2014-2018 transcripts, extended

datasets.name: Interactive conversations
datasets.size: 100 conversations per model, 14-28 turns (>=700 labelled turns); DialoGPT 300; Cleverbot 195; XiaoIce 119; Mitsuku 100; human-human 100
datasets.source: crowd workers or internal volunteers chatting freely, starting with 'Hi!'

models.name: Meena
models.architecture: seq2seq Evolved Transformer, 1 encoder block and 13 decoder blocks, shared embeddings across encoder, decoder and softmax
models.context: 128 tokens encoder, 128 decoder (256 combined); up to 7 context turns

other.largest vanilla Transformer: 32 decoder layers, perplexity 10.7 at same 738k steps

other.decoding: top-K K=10 (own implementation after Wolf et al. 2019), no MMI reranking

training.lr_schedule: constant for first 10k steps, then inverse square root of step number
training.steps: 738k (stated for the ET/Transformer comparison at same steps)
training.regularisation: dropout only; model can overfit the 61B-token set
training.hardware: TPU-v3 Pod, 2,048 cores, 16GB HBM per core

other.ablations: layers, heads, steps, ET vs Transformer, hard vs soft labels (distillation)

inference.decoding: sample-and-rank: sample N independent candidates, return the highest-probability one
inference.samples: N=20 candidates per response; 7 repeat evaluations of best model

parameters.cross-turn repetition rule: remove candidates sharing long common sub-sequences with any earlier turn; threshold not given
parameters.safety layer: extra classifier filtering at serving time for full Meena

metrics.name: Sensibleness
metrics.definition: % of responses crowd workers label as making sense in context

metrics.name: Specificity
metrics.definition: % of responses labelled specific to context; non-sensible counts as not specific

metrics.name: SSA
metrics.definition: simple average of sensibleness and specificity

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: test-set next-token perplexity, lower better, minimum 1

eval.protocol: 5 crowd workers per item with majority vote; static (MTB) and interactive; regression R2 of SSA on perplexity; agreement and Krippendorff alpha reported; 7 repeats for SD

availability.data: conversations with Meena and other bots on github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/meena/

limits: Static set has 1-3 turn contexts, mostly Turing-test and social chat; no deep QA, maths or commonsense-challenge contexts
Interactive conversations are 14-28 turns, weighted to greetings and endings, too short for memory or deep topics
Unclear whether the linear perplexity-SSA trend continues at lower perplexity
XiaoIce and Mitsuku evaluated via web apps with volunteers, XiaoIce state not reset, shared account; XiaoIce optimises engagement so Meena is at an advantage
DialoGPT used own decoder; Mitsuku web version differs from Loebner-winning one
Humans in the human baseline knew they were talking to a human
Full Meena evaluated with an extra safety classifier; training data and model not released
No empathy, humor or reasoning measured
